Founder Letter

01

Keeping it simple.

The Velardos never played tennis. We played golf.

So on the pro tour, up against players who grew up with a racquet in their hand, I had to keep it simple: the baby block, for the hard balls, and the boring drop, for the low balls. Anybody can learn them, and they lead to the best thing in social pickleball: the long points we share.

And when you really understand the game, you'll see you can get very good at pickleball with just these two simple techniques.

02

Why it matters.

By far the biggest value our members get from NEPC is relational, not individual: the shared moments on the court, and the friendships that grow from them.

Pickleball is full of silly moments that make it easy to open up together:

  • hitting the ball that was going out,
  • forgetting the score,
  • you and your partner both watching the ball go right down the middle.

But one shared experience beats them all, hands down:

the long points.

And you don't have to be a competitive player to get them. At our fun, social events, the baby block and the boring drop are the easiest way to have more fun: you stay in more points, you pop up fewer balls, and you get more of the long rallies everyone talks about afterward.

Most of us aren't training for the pro tour, and we don't need to play like the pros. (If you are, we have players and coaches who have done it, and we can help with that too.) There's an easier way to play, made for people who didn't grow up with a racquet: simple technique, and the easiest path to long points with your friends.

NEPC is an equal opportunity club. We love our bangers and our players with high-level racquet skills, just as much as long-point style players like myself.

My mission is for every NEPC member to get the baby block and the boring drop down solid!

Become a member

Included in your membership

  • Two printed charts.One for each skill, from the front desk. Each breaks the skill into its pieces, so you always know what to work on next.
  • Play with the owners.Look for the ladders and social events Samara and I are playing in. When there's time between games, ask me and I'll show you where you are on each chart. The work is up to you.
  • Gamma weighted strips.For every new member, on us, and we'll put them on for you. A little weight helps with both skills.
  • Social events.Made for exactly this: long rallies, together. And something new: when I notice a member within any of our skill buckets who has their baby block and boring drop down solid, I'll ask them to partner with me and stack and we'll challenge higher level member teams. Let's go!
03

Together.

A lot of smart people say pickleball clubs are in the hospitality business. That's true, but I believe we're much more than that. We're a different kind of business: a community.

Everyone has something to contribute. Mine is spreading these two skills across the club. What's yours? It can be simple:

  • Sub into a game
  • Host an event
  • Get on court with a developing player
  • And most important of allInvite a friend.

To my boring friends who already have both skills: thank you. The more of us who do, the longer the points and the more fun the games.

Come play
with us.

We'd love to play with you.

Dave and Samara
